decision: reuse existing bundle files only after a direct-file digest match; otherwise use the existing verified download and replacement path

redGreen.red: existing corrupt bytes were skipped and returned as successful instead of being replaced by the declared healthy bytes
redGreen.green: controlled and progress APIs each replace corrupt direct-file and archive-member fixtures through actual loopback HTTP; four successful transfers
redGreen.reuse: second direct-file call succeeds offline after rehash; archive member cannot be verified with archive digest, so a second call attempts download and reports the closed-server request error without changing healthy member bytes
redGreen.unknown: files without a declared direct digest are downloaded rather than reused
redGreen.fixtures: red fixture removed by exact owned name and corrupt-byte marker; passing fixtures clean themselves

review.method: separate read-only review of both download entry points, model-manager caller and atomic replacement boundary
checks: both APIs share one reuse predicate and existing streaming SHA implementation
archive SHA is never compared to extracted member bytes or treated as its proof
known-valid direct files avoid network; uppercase expected digests retain case-insensitive comparison
unreadable existing direct files propagate actual IO failure rather than a guessed digest result
mismatch leaves old bytes present until the existing download validates and renames its temporary file
cancellation checkpoints and source/checksum failure propagation remain in the existing download path
no new dependency, global digest cache, force-install UI or overwrite of active installed profiles
limits: real small HTTP/archive fixtures, not a new model-quality or throughput acceptance run
archive members may download again during a partial-install retry because schema v1 stores only the archive digest
does not add repair/reinstall for a fully installed model or guarantee runtime file immutability
